items.followUp: A floating object displaces 3 kg of water. What is the mass of the object?

rubric.why: The principle states that the weight of a floating body equals the weight of the fluid it displaces.
rubric.description: States the equality between the weight of the floating body and the weight of the displaced fluid.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for clearly stating both weights and their equality.

modelAnswer: A floating body displaces a fluid whose weight is equal to the weight of the body.

items.followUp: What instrument is used to measure the temperature of a body?

rubric.why: A thermometer is used to measure a quantity.
rubric.description: States that a thermometer is used to measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the measuring function.

rubric.why: Temperature is the quantity measured by a thermometer.
rubric.description: Identifies temperature as the measured quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming temperature.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is used to measure the temperature of a body.

items.followUp: Derive the first equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

accept: s=area under the speed time graph
displacement=area under the speed time graph
area under the speed time graph
rubric.why: The area under a speed-time graph gives the displacement.
rubric.description: Relates displacement to the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the area as displacement.

rubric.why: The graph's area is a trapezium with parallel sides u and v and width t.
rubric.description: Uses the trapezium area to express displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the trapezium area or writing its correct expression.

rubric.why: Substituting the first equation of motion into the area expression enables the derivation.
rubric.description: Substitutes v = u + at into the displacement expression.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.why: This is the derived second equation of motion.
rubric.description: Obtains the second equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Let the speed increase uniformly from u to v in time t; displacement s is the area under the speed-time graph.
The region under the graph is a trapezium, so s = ½(u + v)t.
Using v = u + at: s = ½(u + u + at)t.

items.followUp: A 0.4 kg body moves in a circle of radius 0.8 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force.

rubric.why: The mass is correctly recorded in SI units.
rubric.description: Records the mass in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.5 kg.

rubric.why: The radius must be converted from centimetres to metres.
rubric.description: Converts and records the radius in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for r = 0.50 m.

rubric.why: This is the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.description: Gives the correct centripetal-force formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = mv²/r.

rubric.why: The values are correctly substituted into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct numerical substitution.

rubric.why: The calculated centripetal force is 9 N.
rubric.description: Gives the final force with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 9 N.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, v = 3 m s⁻¹, r = 50 cm = 0.50 m.
Substitution: F = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.50 m).

items.followUp: State the two conditions for equilibrium and explain what each condition prevents.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force is the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the first condition of equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: A zero resultant force means there is no linear acceleration.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the first condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking it to no linear acceleration or translational equilibrium.

rubric.why: Zero resultant torque is the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the second condition of equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque or moment is zero.

rubric.why: A zero resultant torque means there is no angular acceleration.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the second condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking it to no angular acceleration or rotational equilibrium.

modelAnswer: First condition (translational equilibrium): the resultant force on the body must be zero, so the body has no linear acceleration.
Second condition (rotational equilibrium): the resultant torque about any point must be zero, so the body has no angular acceleration.

items.followUp: A wooden cube of sides 20 cm each is completely submerged in water. Calculate the upthrust acting on it.

rubric.why: The cube's side length is converted to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the side length to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the side as 0.10 m.

rubric.why: The volume of the submerged cube is 0.001 m³.
rubric.description: Calculates the cube's volume in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume or calculation.

rubric.why: Upthrust equals the weight of displaced water, expressed as ρVg.
rubric.description: States the buoyancy principle or its formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct principle or formula.

rubric.why: The density of water, volume, and gravitational field strength are substituted.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values for water density, volume and g.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly substituting the values.

rubric.why: The upthrust is 10 N using g = 10 m s⁻², or 9.8 N using g = 9.8 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Gives the upthrust with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct result using the corresponding value of g.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 10 cm = 0.10 m; density of water ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³; g = 10 m s⁻².
Volume of cube: V = (0.10 m)³ = 0.001 m³.
Upthrust = weight of displaced water = ρVg.
